messages:
sam: Hey, noticed a bunch of pods in eu-west3 failing readiness right after the GPU scale-up at 11:05 UTC. Errors look like connection resets, lots of user traffic to model-registry.

nina: saw spike in NAT table usage around the same time, crt alerted. Can you paste `conntrack` counts?

sam: ran `conntrack -S` on node gpu-node-17, key bits:
```
# conntrack -S
entries: 65534
searched: 123456
found: 123000
lost: 0
```

leo: 65k entries, that matches nf_conntrack_max hitting the cap (we set it to 65k in that az).

anya: why would scale-up cause a burst? pods spawn, prefetches to external model-registry, RDMA handshake failures caused reconnect loops?

sam: timeline looked like: new GPU nodes join -> init containers hit registry to pull weights -> simultaneous parallel pulls + control-plane probes -> many short-lived TCP connections -> conntrack fills, pods behind service IPs start getting SNAT failures and healthchecks time out.

kevin: also saw MTU mismatch logs on one host, some RDMA paths falling back to TCP which multiplied connection attempts. That probably amplified ephemeral port churn.

infra-bot: deploy detected: scaleup/gpu-pool -> 2025-10-14T11:04:32Z; alerts: conntrack-near-cap, pod-probe-failures-eu-west3.

nina: immediate mitigation: can we throttle parallelism of prefetch/boot pulls? Or stagger node bootstrap?

leo: short term: increase `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` and bump `conntrack` hashsize, and tune gc thresholds. Example sysctl to try: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144`

anya: agree, but increasing table just masks the root cause. We should also limit parallel outgoing connections from init scripts and make registry pulls use HTTP keep-alive (reuse sockets).

sam: I pushed a quick change to the GPU-init job to add `--concurrency 4` for downloads, rolling out to eu-west3 now.

kevin: rolling kernel conntrack tuning as well: set `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` lower for our short-lived bursts and enable `nf_conntrack_generic_timeout` reductions.

nina: longer-term: consider eBPF service routing (no SNAT for clusterIP) or ensure `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` for ingress to avoid SNAT explosion. Also evaluate keeping a local model-cache on node to avoid massive egress.

anya: did we confirm which entries dominated the table? I ran `conntrack -L | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 6` and saw a huge number of `TCP` entries to registry:443 and to `10.88.x.x:3000` (our sidecar probes).

sam: logs: ```
$ conntrack -L | grep registry.example.com | wc -l
48220
```

kevin: ok that's huge. We should also check ephemeral port range on nodes: `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` - might be too small causing port reuse/ TIME_WAIT pileup.

leo: action list:
- increase nf_conntrack_max to 262k on eu-west3 hosts (sam/kevin)
- roll GPU-init concurrency change (sam)
- add short-term conntrack gc tuning (kevin)
- investigate MTU/RDMA fallback logs and fix path MTU on affected racks (anya)
- evaluate eBPF/no-SNAT service routing for heavy east-west model traffic (nina/leo)

infra-bot: escalation: oncall @kevin has been paged (priority: P2)

oncall-bot: page delivered to kevin at 11:12 UTC

kevin: applying nf_conntrack_max bump now on a canary host, will watch metrics for 10m. Also enabling `conntrack` top-up script if > 70% used to log and notify.

sam: after bump and staggered boot, pod readiness failures dropped to near-zero and model pulls spread over ~8 minutes instead of a 30s spike. Still want postmortem and a config change to defaults.

nina: please add notes to the incident doc: link to `/incidents/2025-10-14-eu-west3-snat-surge` and include commands we ran and the tuned sysctls.

anya: for the postmortem: quantify cost of the extra connections (egress + lost requests) and propose a default init concurrency for GPU nodes.

sam: will open the PR with the init concurrency and add monitoring alert for registry conntrack ratio > 0.6. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
